summary:
Two pointers from both ends: move each pointer past non-letters, then swap the two letters they point at and
step both inward. Non-letters never move, and the letters end up reversed. O(n) time, in place.

question.md:
Reverse only the letters of `text`; every other character keeps its exact position.

- **Letters** are A–Z and a–z; digits, punctuation and spaces stay put.
- **Up to 10⁵ characters.**

think.md:
`ab-cd3e!f` becomes `fe-dc3b!a`: the letters a, b, c, d, e, f come out as f, e, d, c, b, a, while `-`, `3` and `!`
stay where they were.

Reversing means the first letter swaps with the last letter, the second with the second-to-last, and so on.
Two pointers find those pairs directly, skipping the characters that don't take part.

approaches.title: Collect and write back

idea.md: Copy the letters out in order. Walk the text again; at each letter position, write the next letter from the end of the copy.

build: Rebuild the text, taking letters from the back of the gathered list.

lines.text: The letters, in their original order.
Letter positions get letters from the back of the list; other characters are copied as they are.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the gathered letters.

walk.title: Collect the letters, then write them back in reverse order into the letter positions.

limits.md: Uses an extra copy of the letters. Swapping from both ends does the same reversal in place.

idea.md: `i` at the start, `j` at the end. Advance `i` past non-letters, pull `j` back past non-letters; when both sit on letters, swap them and move both inward.

lines.text: A mutable copy (strings are immutable in Python and Java), with pointers at both ends.
Non-letters stay where they are: step over them.
Both pointers are on letters: swap and move inward.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** every step moves a pointer. **Space O(1)** beyond the copy of the text.

walk.title: Two pointers from the ends: skip non-letters on each side, then swap the two letters.

takeaways.md:
- **Reversal = swapping from both ends.** Filtering (only letters) just adds skip steps.
- Characters that don't participate never move, so skipping them keeps them in place.
- In C/C++, cast to `unsigned char` before calling `isalpha`.
